correctness.rationale: For any n-state permutation DFA the root transition group has at most n! elements; the witness generators make this S_n and the singleton initial-final state ensures the original DFA is minimal. For prime p>=3, the set B_p of permutations whose p-th power fixes zero comprises cycle lengths one or p. The explicit two-case stabilizer lemma constructs, for every nonidentity h, a permutation g in B_p with gh outside B_p: a p-cycle through zero for h fixing zero, or a transposition separating predecessor/successor on h’s p-cycle (or identity if h already outside). This makes the right stabilizer trivial and all n! root group states distinguishable by continuation. Unary groups are proper cyclic subgroups of noncyclic S_n. The independent finite checker tests every nonidentity h through n=8 and performs direct root-DFA minimization through n=6.

value.rationale: An infinite two-parameter exact extremum (n states, every odd prime p<=n) for a natural regular-language operation; factorial deterministic blow-up is achieved with the provably smallest alphabet. The structural right-stabilizer lemma explains the phenomenon beyond the known square root and offers a reusable distinction criterion. This is not a small isolated finite check or merely a renamed theorem.
